task_description: Help me draft an email from our CEO to department heads about a company-wide hiring freeze — the CEO is direct but empathetic, and the CFO and board chair will be CC'd.

rubric_used.user_goals_summary: Writes emails that navigate organizational power dynamics with precision. Every word is chosen for how it lands with the primary recipient AND the CC'd audience. Treats email as a tool of organizational choreography, not just communication.

rubric.name: CC Audience Awareness
rubric.description: Every CC'd person is there for a reason, and the email is crafted knowing they will read it. The primary recipient gets the ask; the CC'd audience gets a deliberate signal — accountability, visibility, or alignment.

dimensions.label: Each CC'd person receives a specific signal from the email (accountability, awareness, endorsement)
Nothing in the email reveals information inappropriate for any CC'd reader
The primary recipient and their specific ask are unambiguous despite the CC'd audience
The CC list itself sends a message — the choice of who is included is deliberate

rubric.name: Directive Clarity
rubric.description: Non-negotiable requests use direct language, never conditional framing. 'Please submit by Friday' not 'Would you be able to submit by Friday?' Conditional language is reserved exclusively for genuinely optional items.

dimensions.label: Required actions do not use 'if possible', 'would you be able to', or 'it would be great if'
Truly optional items use optionality language to distinguish them from requirements
The level of directness matches the sender's authority relative to the recipient

rubric.name: Recipient-Interest Framing
rubric.description: Requests are positioned as serving the recipient's interest, even when the ask primarily benefits the sender. The reframe must be genuine — not a transparent manipulation.

dimensions.label: The email explains how the ask serves the recipient or their team, not just the sender
The benefit framing is credible — the recipient would agree it serves them if asked
Avoids 'we need this for our planning' when 'this helps your team plan' is more accurate

rubric.name: Voice Matching
rubric.description: When writing on behalf of an executive, the email sounds like that person — mirroring their vocabulary, sentence length, and communication style — not like a generic professional email.

dimensions.label: Uses words and phrases the named executive would actually use
Sentence length, formality level, and directness match the executive's established pattern
The email could not be attributed to 'any senior leader' — it has a specific voice

rubric_used.coaching_notes: Carmen treats every email as having two audiences — the TO and the CC — and writes for both simultaneously. Non-negotiable: conditional language is never used for non-negotiable requests. Will reject drafts that sound generically polished rather than like the specific executive's voice.

Subject: Hiring Pause Effective Immediately — Action Required from All Department Heads

---

To: Department Heads
CC: [CFO Name], [Board Chair Name]

---

Team,

Effective today, we are pausing all external hiring across the company. This includes open requisitions, roles in final interview stages, and any positions not yet posted. If an offer has already been extended, contact [CFO Name] directly before proceeding.

I want to be straightforward with you about why.

The current environment requires us to be more disciplined about how we deploy capital — and headcount is our single largest cost. This pause gives each of your teams something valuable: a clear signal that leadership is protecting the resources you already have. We are not cutting. We are stopping before we have to.

Here is what I need from you by end of day Friday:

- A list of any open requisitions currently in process, including stage and hiring manager
- Any offers extended but not yet accepted
- Roles you consider operationally critical — flag these separately, with a one-paragraph business case

That last item matters. If a role is genuinely essential to your team's ability to function, make the case. I will review exceptions personally with [CFO Name].

I know this creates friction. Some of you have been working for months to fill positions that are real gaps, not wish-list roles. I don't take that lightly. What I'm asking you to do now — document, prioritize, advocate for your teams — is exactly the work that will position you well when this pause lifts.

We will regroup as a leadership team on [date] to review the full picture.

Thank you for moving quickly on this.

[CEO Name]

Subject: Hiring Pause Effective Immediately — Action Required from All Department Heads

---

To: Department Heads
CC: [CFO Name], [Board Chair Name]

---

Team,

Effective today, we are pausing all external hiring. Every open req, every role in final rounds, every position not yet posted — paused. If an offer is already out, call [CFO Name] before you do anything else.

I'll tell you exactly where this is coming from.

We are in a moment that rewards restraint. The board and I have been aligned on this for several weeks — [Board Chair Name] has been a clear voice that protecting our current team and our current runway is the right call right now. This isn't a reactive decision. It's a deliberate one, and it's the right one.

Here's what that means for you: we are not cutting. The people on your teams today are not at risk. What we're doing is stopping before we'd ever have to make that call. That's worth something.

By end of day Friday, I need three things from you:

- Every open requisition in process — stage, hiring manager, timeline
- Any offers extended but not yet accepted
- Roles you believe are operationally essential — listed separately, with a short business case for each

On that third item: if a role is a genuine gap, advocate for it. I will sit down with [CFO Name] and review every exception personally. Make your case clearly and I'll give it a real look.

I know some of you have spent months getting the right candidates to the finish line. That's not lost on me. What I'm asking you to do right now — document what you have, prioritize ruthlessly, fight for what actually matters — is the same discipline that's going to serve your teams well on the other side of this.

We'll regroup as a leadership team on [date].

Move fast on this.

[CEO Name]

---

To: Department Heads
CC: [CFO Name], [Board Chair Name]

---

Team,

As of today, we are pausing all external hiring. Every open req, every role in final rounds, every position not yet posted — paused. If an offer is already out the door, stop and call [CFO Name] before you take another step.

Here is the plain version of why.

We are protecting what we have built. [Board Chair Name] and the board have been direct with me: the organizations that come out of this period strongest are the ones that defend their core and don't overextend. I agree. This pause is not a hedge — it is a choice, and it is the right one.

What that means for your teams: we are not cutting. The people sitting in your organizations today are not at risk. We are stopping now precisely so we never have to have that conversation.

By end of day Friday, I need three things from you:

- Every open requisition currently in process — stage, hiring manager, where it stands
- Any offers that have been extended but not yet accepted
- Roles you consider essential to your team's ability to operate — flagged separately, with a clear business case

On that last item: if a role is a real gap, make the case for it. [CFO Name] and I will review every exception together. Write it like you mean it and I will give it a serious look.

I know what I am asking. Some of you have spent months building pipelines and getting the right people to the finish line. That work is not wasted — it is exactly what will let you move quickly when this pause lifts. Document what you have. Prioritize hard. Fight for what your team genuinely needs.

We will regroup as a leadership team on [date].

Move quickly.

[CEO Name]
